hero.headline: Draft picks power new-look St. Lucie Mets in 14-6 rout of Dunedin
hero.teaser: Four 2026 draft picks combined for nine hits and three home runs, while Clay Holmes threw four scoreless innings in a rehab appearance.
hero.body:
Four members of the New York Mets’ 2026 draft class made immediate impacts Tuesday night as the St. Lucie Mets overwhelmed the Dunedin Blue Jays 14-6 at TD Ballpark.

Aiden Robbins, Ryan Tayman, John Smith III and Kooper Schulte combined to go 9-for-17 with three home runs, two doubles, seven RBIs and seven runs scored in their professional debuts. The St. Lucie lineup also featured Yovanny Rodriguez and Wyatt Vincent, who made their team debuts after being promoted from the Florida Complex League.

The revamped offense provided more than enough support for New York Mets pitcher Clay Holmes, who moved his rehabilitation assignment from Triple-A Syracuse to the Florida State League because of predicted bad weather in New York.

Holmes, recovering from a right fibula injury, scattered two singles and two walks over four scoreless innings. He struck out three and threw 59 pitches.

Tayman gave St. Lucie a 2-0 lead in the second inning by hitting a two-run home run on the first swing of his professional career. The ninth-round selection out of Cal Poly finished 4-for-5 with a homer, a double, two singles, three runs scored and two RBIs.

Robbins, a third-round pick from Texas, drove an RBI double off the center-field wall in the third inning for his first professional hit.

The Mets added three runs in the fourth. Cole Mathis delivered a sacrifice fly before Marco Vargas lined a two-run double off the left-field wall against Dunedin starter Blake Purnell, extending the lead to 6-0.

Smith, a 19th-round pick from UCF, hit a two-run homer off Purnell in the fifth inning for his first professional hit. He homered again in the ninth and finished 2-for-5 with three RBIs.

Austin Warren, beginning a rehabilitation assignment for a right forearm strain, pitched a scoreless fifth inning with one strikeout and induced a double play. He was credited with the win.

Dunedin scored four runs against Tyler McLoughlin in the sixth, but Ernesto Mercedes stopped the rally with consecutive strikeouts. Mercedes then retired the Blue Jays in order in the seventh and added two more strikeouts.

Elian Peña hit a two-run homer in the eighth, and Robbins added an RBI single to push St. Lucie’s lead to 11-4.

The Mets scored three more runs in the ninth on Smith’s second homer, a bases-loaded walk by Julio Zayas and an RBI single from Vargas. Vargas finished 3-for-5 with three RBIs.

Schulte, a 20th-round pick from Iowa, went 1-for-3 with a single, a walk, a hit-by-pitch and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs in his St. Lucie debut, while Vincent went 1-for-4 with a double, a walk and a run.

The Mets improved to 12-18 in the second half and 45-51 overall. Dunedin fell to 14-16 in the second half and 44-51 overall.

The teams continue the series Wednesday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Martin County Fire Rescue could lose 116 firefighters, close stations if property tax reform passes
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli warned commissioners Tuesday that proposed property tax reform on the November ballot could force sweeping cuts to fire and rescue operations. The reform would expand homestead exemptions, potentially reducing the department's budget and forcing the loss of as many as 116 firefighters over the next two years.

The potential cuts outlined by Cianciulli include closing firehouses, ending hazmat, dive, and technical rescue programs, grounding the department's critical care helicopter, and using firefighting tools past their operational lifetime. The department could also be forced to implement a no-overtime policy, resulting in randomized brownouts of stations and longer emergency response times across Martin County. Commissioners also warned that station closures could result in higher homeowner insurance premiums for residents who live more than five miles from the nearest fire station.

Residents who attended the commission meeting Tuesday expressed mixed reactions. Commissioners Edward Ciampi and Eileen Vargas offered differing views on how to respond if the reform passes, with Ciampi suggesting belt tightening and slashing budgets elsewhere. County documents show that about 93% of the Fire Rescue budget is dedicated to personnel, leaving few options to absorb the projected revenue loss.

No decisions were made Tuesday. The presentation was an opportunity to gather information so the county can plan accordingly ahead of the November vote. Voters will have the final say on the constitutional amendment during the November general election.

cards.headline: Florida carries out first double execution in more than 60 years, including second-oldest inmate in U.S. history
cards.teaser: Florida on Tuesday became the first state in nearly a decade to carry out two executions in a single day, putting to death an 80-year-old man who was the second.
cards.body:
Florida on Tuesday became the first state in nearly a decade to carry out two executions in a single day, putting to death an 80-year-old man who was the second-oldest inmate known to receive a lethal injection in modern U.S. history. Dominick Anthony Occhicone was pronounced dead at 6:13 p.m. at Florida State Prison near Starke following a three-drug injection. His execution came nearly five hours after James Aren Duckett, 68, a former police officer convicted of raping and drowning 11-year-old Teresa McAbee in 1987, received a lethal dose in the same death chamber. Duckett was pronounced dead at 1:19 p.m.

Gov. Ron DeSantis, who has the authority under Florida law to set execution dates, decided earlier this month to carry out both executions on the same day. The lethal injections just hours apart were the first nearly back-to-back executions since Arkansas put two men to death three hours apart in 2017. DeSantis has made Florida's death chamber the nation's busiest at the end of his final term, saying too many families have waited too long to see justice. Florida Department of Corrections records show multiple executions on a single day were more common in the past, the last being in 1964.

Occhicone, who was convicted of fatally shooting his ex-girlfriend's parents in June 1986, is the oldest known prisoner executed in Florida since modern record-keeping began a century ago. Nationwide, an older inmate, 83-year-old Walter Moody Jr., received a lethal injection in Alabama in 2018 for a wave of mail bombs in 1989 that killed a federal judge and wounded a Black civil rights attorney. Asked if he had any final words, Occhicone thanked his Christian brothers for visiting him over the years and apologized to the families of the victims and his own family. Duckett declined to make a final statement.

Florida has now conducted 12 executions in 2026, more than all other states combined. Nationwide, a total of 19 executions have been carried out this year. DeSantis, who leaves office in January, oversaw a record 19 executions last year, more in a single year than any other Florida governor since the U.S. reinstatement of the death penalty in 1976. Another execution in Florida is set for August. The U.S. Supreme Court denied last appeals from both men Tuesday. All Florida executions are by injection of a sedative, a paralytic and a drug that stops the heart, according to the Department of Corrections.

cards.headline: Martin County projects $16.5 million annual Fire Rescue budget loss under proposed homestead exemption
cards.teaser: Martin County Fire Rescue projects its annual budget would decline by $9.5 million in the first year if voters approve expanded homestead exemptions in November.
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Rescue projects its annual budget would decline by $9.5 million in the first year under a proposed expansion of Florida's homestead exemption. By the second year, the annual loss would reach $16.5 million, a 22% reduction from the department's current budget. Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli presented the planning exercise during Tuesday's commission meeting.

Under the scenario, Fire Rescue could close Station 18 on Britt Road, Station 33 in Hobe Sound, and Station 23 on Kanner Highway. The department could be forced to lay off as many as 116 firefighters by the second year, equivalent to one of the department's three shifts. The funding loss could force Martin County to eliminate specialized teams responsible for hazardous materials incidents, technical rescues and dive operations.

Cianciulli pointed to the deadly Camp Mystic flooding in Texas as an example of delays that can occur when a community must rely on outside resources. In an interview after the meeting, Cianciulli said they had to call for outside assets, a 14 hour response to start mitigating that scene. He said Martin County is in a position where if any incident happens, they are able to do an immediate mitigation without wasting any second.

cards.headline: Martin County Fire Rescue warns station brownouts, higher insurance premiums possible under tax amendment
cards.teaser: Martin County Commissioner James Blake Capps said a no-overtime policy for fire rescue personnel could result in randomized brownouts of stations if the tax amendment passes.
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Rescue projects it could lose 116 firefighters over the next two years about one third of its workforce because of reduced property tax revenue tied to a proposed constitutional amendment on the November ballot. County leaders warned the proposed cuts could lead to longer emergency response times and affect specialized emergency services provided throughout Martin County. Fire Rescue leaders discussed potential operational changes if those revenue reductions occur.

Commissioner James Blake Capps said there would have to be a no-overtime policy for all fire rescue personnel. That doesn't sound so bad initially, but the consequences mean no backfilling of stations with personnel, which would result in randomized brownouts of stations. Capps also said if the county shuts down three fire stations, a lot of people would end up paying more for homeowner's insurance because they would be farther than five miles away from a fire station.

County leaders have previously said the department has few options to absorb the projected revenue loss because about 93% of the Fire Rescue budget is dedicated to personnel. No vote on firefighter layoffs or fire station closures was expected during Tuesday's meeting. Voters will have the final say on the constitutional amendment during the November general election.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie men flee police at 80 mph, one found hiding on roof of occupied home
cards.teaser: Two men led Port St. Lucie police on a high-speed chase before abandoning their car and fleeing on foot Monday, with one suspect found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.
cards.body:
A suspected drunk driver fled Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone before he and his passenger abandoned their car and ran. According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, officers attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving on Southwest Becker Road. Instead of pulling over, the driver accelerated and weaved in and out of traffic, ignoring traffic signs and signals.

The driver and passenger abandoned the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue before fleeing on foot. A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter. Both suspects were located, including one who was found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.

The suspects were identified as Joseph Gary Harris, 42, and Bryan Shawn Baker, 46. Harris was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence, and loitering or prowling. Baker was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

cards.body:

hero.headline: 3 arrested in Fort Pierce after 3-month-old dies from dehydration and malnutrition
hero.body:
A 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in August 2025 after living in a Fort Pierce mobile home with boarded windows, exposed electrical wiring and cockroaches, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Nicole Maxwell, 27, the infant's mother, Robert Maxwell, 61, the child's grandfather, and Vikki Koon, 38, Robert Maxwell's girlfriend, were arrested and charged with aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse nearly a year after the death.

The investigation began in August 2025 when Robert Maxwell and Koon brought the deceased infant to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. The medical examiner determined the child died from dehydration and malnutrition, with court documents describing the infant's ribs as more prominent than its stomach. Koon told deputies she fed the infant only twice a day and when she ran out of formula, she fed the child watered-down milk with baby cereal mixed in. The infant lived primarily with Robert Maxwell and Koon at their mobile home in the 800 block of Silverstream Circle in Fort Pierce while Nicole Maxwell lived at her boyfriend's home in Vero Beach.

Detective Jennifer Diaz, who worked the case, said the mobile home was extremely hot with a bug infestation, lack of food, and unsafe conditions for walking. A neighbor named Suzan said she witnessed the conditions firsthand and described the home as unlivable. Suzan said other children from the home would come to her asking for water, appearing thirsty, unbathed and wearing the same clothes every day. Nicole Maxwell's four other children, ranging in age from 2 to 10 years old, were living in the mobile home and have been placed in foster care through the Department of Children and Families.

Detective Diaz said the investigation took nearly a year because the case required outside experts and additional testing. Koon and Robert Maxwell are being held in the St. Lucie County Jail each on $1.5 million bond. Nicole Maxwell was arrested on July 23 at a home in the 300 block of 12th Street SW in Vero Beach and is being held in the Indian River County Jail on no bond. Diaz emphasized the importance of reporting suspicious activity to protect children, saying tips are instrumental to keeping children safe.

cards.headline: Man forced to withdraw cash at gunpoint at Fort Pierce Wells Fargo ATM
cards.teaser: Two men forced a customer to withdraw cash at a Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce Sunday night before fleeing on foot. The suspects remain at large despite a K-9 and drone search.
cards.body:
A man using a Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce was forced to withdraw cash at gunpoint Sunday at about 8:38 p.m., according to the Fort Pierce Police Department. Two men approached the victim, and one of them displayed a gun concealed in his waistband before forcing the victim to withdraw an unknown amount of cash. The suspects fled the scene on foot.

Officers responded to the scene, established a perimeter, and used a K-9 and drone to search for the suspects, but the suspects were not located. Police described the suspects as two men in their early 20s, about 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighing about 170 pounds. The armed suspect was last seen wearing jeans and a gray hooded sweatshirt.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie opens $28.8 million police training facility
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie cut the ribbon on a 54,283-square-foot police training center featuring a 20-lane indoor firearms range, tactical shoot house and virtual simulation theater.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie officially opened a 54,283-square-foot, $28.8 million police training center on July 24 on the grounds of City Hall, just northwest of the police department. Mayor Shannon Martin said the project is about making sure officers have the space, training and resources needed to serve the community at the highest level. The facility took four years to construct.

The three-story facility includes a 20-lane, 9,508-square-foot indoor firearms range featuring an integrated MILO live-fire scenario system, a 2,848-square-foot tactical shoot house with configurable rooms for realistic scenario-based training, and a MILO Virtual Simulation Theater for immersive decision-making and de-escalation exercises. The facility also includes a dedicated defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology, a multi-purpose training room for classroom instruction and conferences, and three floors of office space supporting the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division with 19 offices and 86 workstations. Officer Brittany McNally said the facility will reduce recurring costs from sending officers to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for extensive training while allowing the department to train more efficiently and effectively.

Witnesses provided a description of the driver, allowing officers to review surveillance footage and locate Alvarenga Ramirez several blocks away, where police said he was attempting to hide.

No one was injured in the crash. Alvarenga Ramirez was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail on charges of DUI, leaving the scene of an accident with property damage, and resisting arrest without violence.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie bans gas station on 9.4-acre Tradition commercial parcel after resident concerns
hero.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council unanimously approved an ordinance on July 13 that permanently prohibits construction of a gas station on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Drive in the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development. The council vote was the second and final reading of the 16th amendment to the Tradition MPUD, codifying a restriction that bars any current or future owner from developing a service station on the site.

The amendment changes the parcel's designation from residential to commercial, clearing the way for retail and office development while addressing concerns raised by Heritage Oaks at Tradition residents about traffic and congestion. Winding River Crosstown LLC requested permission to convert what had been planned as Phase 3 of the Heritage Oaks residential development into commercial property. During the initial May 26 quasi-judicial hearing, Vice Mayor Jolien Caraballo and other council members noted increasing congestion along the commercial corridor and asked staff to determine whether gas stations could be eliminated as a permitted use.

Several Heritage Oaks residents urged the council at the June 22 hearing to reject the land-use change, citing concerns about increased traffic, noise and neighborhood impacts. The council voted 4-0 to approve the commercial designation on first reading after the developer agreed to permanently relinquish the right to build a gas station. City planner Bridget Kean said the updated development plan specifies that while service stations remain a permitted use elsewhere within the mixed-use area, they are prohibited on Parcel 11A. Before any mass grading begins, the developer must install a fence along the southern property line to prevent construction access through Southwest Glenbrook Drive, which connects to Heritage Oaks. An architectural wall and landscape buffering must be completed along the southeastern and southern boundaries before the first building permit is issued for vertical construction.

Councilman Anthony Bonna defended the public process and said expanding commercial development will benefit residents by broadening the city's tax base. Councilman David Pickett said he was excited about the residential-to-commercial conversion. Mayor Shannon Martin asked staff to confirm that the prohibition would remain with the property regardless of ownership. Kean confirmed the restriction is now written directly into the Tradition MPUD documents, ensuring no future owner can develop a gas station on the parcel.

cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council voted unanimously July 13 to permanently prohibit a gas station from being built on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstow
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council voted unanimously July 13 to permanently prohibit a gas station from being built on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Drive. The council approved the second and final reading of the 16th amendment to the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development, codifying a restriction that bars any current or future owner from developing a service station on the site. The amendment changes the parcel's designation from residential to commercial, paving the way for retail and office development while addressing residents' concerns about traffic and congestion.

 The issue arose after Winding River Crosstown LLC requested permission to convert what had been planned as Phase 3 of the Heritage Oaks at Tradition residential development into commercial property. Vice Mayor Jolien Caraballo and other council members voiced concerns during the initial May 26 hearing that a convenience store with gas pumps would worsen traffic along Crosstown Parkway west of Interstate 95. The council tabled the request to allow staff time to determine whether gas stations could be eliminated as a permitted use on the parcel.

 Several Heritage Oaks residents urged the council at a June 22 hearing to reject the land-use change, citing concerns about increased traffic, noise and neighborhood impacts. The council voted 4-0 to approve the commercial designation on first reading after the developer agreed to permanently relinquish the right to build a gas station. Before any mass grading begins, the developer must install a fence along the southern property line to prevent construction access through Southwest Glenbrook Drive, which connects to Heritage Oaks. An architectural wall and landscape buffering must be completed along the southeastern and southern boundaries before the first building permit is issued for vertical construction.

 Councilman Anthony Bonna defended both the public process and the final compromise. Councilman David Pickett said the city has consistently heard residents oppose additional housing. City planner Bridget Kean confirmed the restriction is now written directly into the Tradition MPUD documents, ensuring no future owner can develop a gas station on the parcel. The unanimous vote ended months of discussion and cleared the way for commercial development on the site.

cards.headline: $70 million K-8 school breaks ground in Fort Pierce, combining three aging St. Lucie County campuses
cards.teaser: A groundbreaking ceremony marked the start of construction on a new K-8 school in Fort Pierce that will combine three St. Lucie County schools into one state-of-the-art facility. T
cards.body:
A groundbreaking ceremony marked the start of construction on a new K-8 school in Fort Pierce that will combine three St. Lucie County schools into one state-of-the-art facility. The new school will be built on land behind Dan McCarty Middle School and is expected to welcome between 1,500 and 1,800 students when it opens. It will consolidate Dan McCarty Middle, St. Lucie Elementary and Lawnwood Elementary into a single campus.

 Superintendent Jon Prince said the project is moving forward on time, on budget and on schedule. Prince said the new facility will feature state-of-the-art technology and serve the north part of St. Lucie County. The decision to consolidate comes as the existing schools show their age.

 All three were built in the 1950s and 1960s. Dan McCarty Middle Principal Latricia Stubbs-James said the wear and tear is visible inside the building and some of the things in there are antiquated.

 The district is funding the $70 million project in part by selling the properties where the three older schools currently stand, offsetting the cost of maintaining aging buildings. Prince said the K-8 model is already proven across the district, which operates 11 other K-8 schools. Attendance is better, test scores are better and grades are better in the K-8s, Prince said.

 Stubbs-James said the K-8 model offers unique benefits for younger students. Kindergarten students can see what it looks like to be an eighth grader at a new K-8, and what it looks like to be a fifth grader, Stubbs-James said. The new Fort Pierce K-8 school is expected to be completed in August 2028.

cards.headline: Martin County fire chief warns property tax reform could force station closures, 116 firefighter layoffs
cards.teaser: Martin County Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli warned commissioners Tuesday that proposed property tax reform on the November ballot could force sweeping cuts to fire and rescue operatio
cards.body:
Martin County Fire Chief Chad Cianciulli warned commissioners Tuesday that proposed property tax reform on the November ballot could force sweeping cuts to fire and rescue operations in Martin County. The reform would expand homestead exemptions, potentially reducing the department's budget and forcing major reductions in service.

 Among the potential cuts outlined by the chief: closing firehouses, ending hazmat, dive, and technical rescue programs, grounding the department's critical care helicopter, and using firefighting tools past their operational lifetime. The department could also be forced to cut as many as 116 firefighters over the next two years. Cianciulli said if incidents go beyond the tools or skill sets on scene, the department would have to call for an outside agency.

 Residents who attended the commission meeting had mixed reactions. One resident said fire service is a valuable thing and other things don't matter as much. Another resident questioned why the idea of cutting personnel pay to make up the shortfall is not part of the options.

 Commissioners also expressed differing views on how to respond if the reform passes. Commissioner Edward Ciampi said the county would be doing more belt tightening and slashing of budgets elsewhere. Commissioner Eileen Vargas said the county only has so many dollars to go around and needs to tighten up.

 No decisions were made Tuesday. The presentation was an opportunity to gather information so the county can plan accordingly ahead of the November vote.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce residents oppose proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe over concerns for St. Lucie County Regional History Museum
cards.teaser: Residents and history advocates in Fort Pierce are raising concerns over a proposed mega yacht marina at Museum Pointe, fearing the development could displace the area's cultural heritage and the St. Lucie County Regional History Museum.
cards.body:
The Port of Fort Pierce master plan draft for 2026 calls for replacing the existing area at Museum Pointe with large floating docks designed for mega yachts, along with a clubhouse, an event center and a water taxi connecting to Harbour Pointe to the north. The plan also proposes relocating the history museum. Terry Howard, a passionate advocate for St. Lucie County's history, expressed disbelief over the proposed changes.

 This is a gem for the area, and I just can't believe they want to put mega yachts here, he said. The museum, it's our culture. It's the center for our culture for this county.

 In a statement, St. Lucie County said that no plans have been approved and feedback from the board will dictate future changes, modifications and clarifications to the draft document. Howard has started a petition opposing the proposed marina, hoping to raise awareness and preserve the location and its natural surroundings. This is just a really fantastic place, and our history is capsulized in this museum here, he said. The draft of the master plan is expected to go before the county commission in August.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County school district cuts 19 workers as Temporary Protected Status expires
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County School District is separating 19 employees from employment today as Temporary Protected Status expires for Haitian workers.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County confirmed 19 district employees will be separated from employment as all school district employees must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Chuck Ridley, director of civic engagement for the Service Employees International Union, said the union expects hundreds of workers statewide to be affected, with nearly 20 employees in the Palm Beach County School District alone.

 Ridley said many of the workers losing TPS protections are bus drivers, custodians, paraprofessionals, food service employees and city workers. He warned that without drivers to pick up students or workers to provide public services, residents will see disruptions in schools, garbage collection and other city functions. The healthcare system could also face staffing shortages, particularly in hospitals and nursing homes that rely heavily on immigrant workers.

 The Florida Healthcare Association said Haitian caregivers are valued members of the long term care workforce, serving as certified nursing assistants, nurses, dietary aides, housekeepers and other essential team members. The association said a disruption to experienced staff could create additional challenges to long term care centers focused on supporting the needs of residents, families and care teams. According to the Lar Management Group, the Haitian community contributes an estimated $1.2 billion to Florida's economy.

hero.headline: Draft picks power new-look St. Lucie Mets in 14-6 rout of Dunedin
hero.teaser: Four 2026 draft picks combined for nine hits and three home runs, while Clay Holmes threw four scoreless innings in a rehab appearance.
hero.body:
Four members of the New York Mets’ 2026 draft class made immediate impacts Tuesday night as the St. Lucie Mets overwhelmed the Dunedin Blue Jays 14-6 at TD Ballpark.

Aiden Robbins, Ryan Tayman, John Smith III and Kooper Schulte combined to go 9-for-17 with three home runs, two doubles, seven RBIs and seven runs scored in their professional debuts. The St. Lucie lineup also featured Yovanny Rodriguez and Wyatt Vincent, who made their team debuts after being promoted from the Florida Complex League.

The revamped offense provided more than enough support for New York Mets pitcher Clay Holmes, who moved his rehabilitation assignment from Triple-A Syracuse to the Florida State League because of predicted bad weather in New York.

Holmes, recovering from a right fibula injury, scattered two singles and two walks over four scoreless innings. He struck out three and threw 59 pitches.

Tayman gave St. Lucie a 2-0 lead in the second inning by hitting a two-run home run on the first swing of his professional career. The ninth-round selection out of Cal Poly finished 4-for-5 with a homer, a double, two singles, three runs scored and two RBIs.

Robbins, a third-round pick from Texas, drove an RBI double off the center-field wall in the third inning for his first professional hit.

The Mets added three runs in the fourth. Cole Mathis delivered a sacrifice fly before Marco Vargas lined a two-run double off the left-field wall against Dunedin starter Blake Purnell, extending the lead to 6-0.

Smith, a 19th-round pick from UCF, hit a two-run homer off Purnell in the fifth inning for his first professional hit. He homered again in the ninth and finished 2-for-5 with three RBIs.

Austin Warren, beginning a rehabilitation assignment for a right forearm strain, pitched a scoreless fifth inning with one strikeout and induced a double play. He was credited with the win.

Dunedin scored four runs against Tyler McLoughlin in the sixth, but Ernesto Mercedes stopped the rally with consecutive strikeouts. Mercedes then retired the Blue Jays in order in the seventh and added two more strikeouts.

Elian Peña hit a two-run homer in the eighth, and Robbins added an RBI single to push St. Lucie’s lead to 11-4.

The Mets scored three more runs in the ninth on Smith’s second homer, a bases-loaded walk by Julio Zayas and an RBI single from Vargas. Vargas finished 3-for-5 with three RBIs.

Schulte, a 20th-round pick from Iowa, went 1-for-3 with a single, a walk, a hit-by-pitch and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs in his St. Lucie debut, while Vincent went 1-for-4 with a double, a walk and a run.

The Mets improved to 12-18 in the second half and 45-51 overall. Dunedin fell to 14-16 in the second half and 44-51 overall.

The teams continue the series Wednesday at TD Ballpark. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware named Florida State League Pitcher of the Week
cards.body:
St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware has been named the Florida State League Pitcher of the Week for the week of July 20-26, Minor League Baseball announced Tuesday. Ware made two appearances last week at Clover Park against Fort Myers, one start on Tuesday and one relief outing on Sunday.

The southpaw combined to pitch 7.0 scoreless innings. He scattered three hits, walked two and struck out 12. The Mets won both games with Ware getting credit for the win on Sunday.

Ware, 22, was drafted by the Mets in the 15th round out of LSU in 2025. He made his pro debut with St. Lucie in April and has been with the team all season.

This is the first FSL Pitcher or Player of the Week award for the Mets this season. The St. Lucie Mets play their home games at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware named FSL Pitcher of the Week
cards.teaser: The 22-year-old left-hander struck out 12 batters over seven scoreless innings in two appearances against Fort Myers.
cards.body:
St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware has been named the Florida State League Pitcher of the Week for July 20-26, Minor League Baseball announced Monday.

 Ware made two appearances against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels at Clover Park, starting Tuesday and returning for a relief outing Sunday. The left-hander combined to throw seven scoreless innings, allowing three hits and two walks while striking out 12 batters.

 The Mets won both games in which Ware appeared. He earned the victory Sunday after pitching four scoreless innings, allowing one hit and one walk and recording a career-high eight strikeouts as St. Lucie rallied for an 11-8 win.

 Ware, 22, was selected by the New York Mets in the 15th round of the 2025 MLB Draft out of LSU. He made his professional debut with St. Lucie in April and has remained with the team throughout the season.

cards.headline: Mets erase 5-0 deficit to beat Mighty Mussels 11-8
cards.teaser: Jeremy Rodriguez went 4-for-4, and Conner Ware struck out a career-high eight as St. Lucie scored eight runs in the second inning.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets erased an early five-run deficit with an eight-run second inning and rallied for an 11-8 win over the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Sunday afternoon at Clover Park.

 Fort Myers won the seven-game series 4-3 and finished the season series with an 8-4 advantage.

 The Mighty Mussels scored three runs in the first inning and two more in the second to build a 5-0 lead. St. Lucie responded with eight runs in the bottom of the second and moved ahead for good.

 Randy Guzman delivered the decisive hit, lining a two-out, two-run single that turned a 5-4 deficit into a 6-5 Mets lead. Julio Zayas followed with a two-run single to extend the advantage to 8-5.

 The Mets added three runs in the third. Elian Peña hit an RBI single, Jacob Reimer drove in a run with a double and Trey Snyder added a sacrifice fly to make it 11-5.

 Conner Ware took over on the mound in the third inning and settled the game down for St. Lucie. Ware pitched four scoreless innings, allowed one hit and one walk, and struck out a career-high eight batters. He struck out the side swinging in the fourth and struck out the side looking in the sixth before earning the win.

 Fort Myers scored three runs in the seventh against Luis Sotillo, who was making his Mets debut. Sotillo recovered by retiring six of the final seven batters he faced and carried the game through the eighth inning.

 Elwis Mijares worked a perfect ninth on six pitches to record his third save.

 Jeremy Rodriguez led the Mets at the plate, going 4-for-4 with a double, an RBI and two runs scored from the No. 9 spot in the order. Zayas and Peña collected two hits apiece.

 Reimer, beginning a minor league rehabilitation assignment for a groin injury, went 1-for-3 with a double, a walk, two RBIs and two runs scored. He played all nine innings at third base.

 The Mets improved to 11-18 in the second half and 44-51 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game road series against the Dunedin Blue Jays on Tuesday. First pitch at TD Ballpark is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Fall Short in 15-14 Loss to Fort Myers
cards.teaser: Randy Guzman hit two home runs and drove in six as the St. Lucie Mets nearly erased an eight-run deficit in a 15-14 loss to Fort Myers.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets nearly erased an eight-run first-inning deficit but fell one run short in a 15-14 loss to the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Saturday night at Clover Park.

 Fort Myers scored eight runs in the opening inning and survived several St. Lucie rallies to earn its third consecutive victory.

 Mets starter Ethan Lanthier was charged with seven runs on five hits and two walks before being removed with two outs in the first inning. Harry Genth delivered a three-run double during the Mussels' early outburst.

 Mets Answer With Five-Run First Inning

 St. Lucie immediately responded with five runs against Fort Myers starter Matt Barr in the bottom of the first. Antonio Jimenez, Branny De Oleo and Simon Juan each recorded RBI hits to cut the deficit to 8-5.

 The Mighty Mussels added three runs against Franyel Diaz in the third inning. Ramiro Dominguez drove in two with a single, and Byron Chourio hit a solo home run to extend the Fort Myers lead to 11-5.

 Trey Snyder helped St. Lucie pull closer in the fourth inning with an unconventional trip around the bases. Snyder's ground-ball single was mishandled by shortstop Quetin Young, who then committed a throwing error that allowed Snyder to score and another run to cross the plate.

 The play cut the Mussels' lead to 11-7.

 Guzman Homers Twice

 Randy Guzman hit a two-run homer against Ramiro Villanueva in the fifth inning to bring the Mets within two runs.

 Villanueva later hit consecutive batters and was ejected. St. Lucie loaded the bases with one out, but reliever Adam Falinski retired Elian Pena on a popout and Snyder on a groundout to preserve the 11-9 Fort Myers advantage.

 Young answered with a three-run home run over the batter's eye in the sixth, pushing the Mussels' lead to 14-9.

 Guzman responded again in the bottom half of the inning, launching a three-run homer to make it 14-12.

 He finished the game 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, six RBIs and two runs scored.

 Ninth-Inning Rally Falls One Run Short

 Ricardo Paez opened the ninth inning with a solo home run that gave Fort Myers a 15-13 lead and provided what proved to be a crucial insurance run.

 Francisco Toledo scored on a wild pitch and throwing error with one out in the bottom of the ninth. Marco Vargas then homered to right field with two outs, pulling St. Lucie within one run at 15-14.

 Brent Francisco struck out Chase Meggers to end the game and record his third save.

 Michael Hilker Jr. earned the win after pitching 2 1/3 scoreless innings of relief for Fort Myers. Lanthier took the loss.

 Jimenez went 2-for-3 with two walks and three runs scored. Vargas, De Oleo and Juan added two hits apiece.

 The Mets fell to 10-18 in the second half and 43-51 overall. The Mighty Mussels improved to 14-14 in the second half and 51-42 overall.

 The teams will conclude their series Sunday at Clover Park. First pitch is scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

cards.headline: Zayas Homers Twice as St. Lucie Mets Cruise Past Mighty Mussels
cards.teaser:
Julio Zayas homered twice and Trey Snyder continued his hot stretch at the plate as the St. Lucie Mets defeated the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels 8-2 Tuesday night at Clover Park.

The
cards.body:
Julio Zayas homered twice and Trey Snyder continued his hot stretch at the plate as the St. Lucie Mets defeated the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels 8-2 Tuesday night at Clover Park.

The victory in the series opener was St. Lucie's fifth win in its last six games.

The Mets held a 1-0 lead through two innings before breaking the game open with four runs against Fort Myers starter Eric Hammond in the third.

Randy Guzman drew a bases-loaded walk to bring home the first run of the inning. Snyder followed with a two-run double before scoring on a throwing error after Antonio Jimenez singled, extending the Mets' lead to 5-0.

Jimenez added a sacrifice fly in the fifth inning to make it 6-0.

Zayas provided the rest of St. Lucie's offense with solo home runs in the sixth and eighth innings. He became the second Mets player this season to record a multi-homer game, joining Guzman.

Zayas finished 3-for-4 with his fifth and sixth home runs of the season.

Snyder also went 3-for-3 with a double, a walk, two RBIs and a run scored. He has collected seven hits over his last two games.

St. Lucie starter Conner Ware pitched three scoreless innings, allowing no runs while striking out four.

Emilio Obispo earned the win after allowing two runs on two hits over four innings. He walked three and struck out three.

Zack Mack pitched a scoreless eighth inning before Elwis Mijares worked the ninth and induced a 4-6-3 double play to end the game.

The Mets improved to 9-14 in the second half and 42-47 overall. The Mighty Mussels fell to 10-13 in the second half and 47-41 overall.

The teams will play the second game of the series Wednesday at Clover Park. The Mets will hold their annual Summer Camp Day, with first pitch scheduled for 11:10 a.m.

cards.headline: Messi bathed Yamal as baby in 2007 photo shoot, now they meet in World Cup final
cards.teaser: A 2007 charity calendar photo shoot paired teenage Lionel Messi with infant Lamine Yamal. Now 19 years later, they face off in Sunday's World Cup final.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Associated Press, took the photos after Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró near Barcelona who wanted to participate.

 Soccer destiny paired her baby boy with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

 Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but interest has skyrocketed with Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain approaching. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation.

 The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in Sunday's final. Monfort, 58, is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey. He said his heart is split and he does not know if he wants Messi or Yamal to win.

hero.headline: Recycled fishing line to be transformed into friendship bracelets at Vero Beach Museum of Art
hero.body:
Discarded fishing line collected from local waterways will be transformed into friendship bracelets during a free Second Saturday program at the Vero Beach Museum of Art on Aug. 8. The museum is partnering with Coastal Connections for hands-on activities beginning at 10 a.m., including docent-led gallery tours and lessons about protecting local marine life.

Coastal Connections will lead the bracelet-making activity in the Laura and Bill Buck Atrium using recycled fishing line collected through the organization's Fishing Line Recycling Program. Participants can also learn about the program and marine conservation efforts. The Vero Beach Museum of Art has adopted the fishing line recycling tube at the Riverside Park boat ramp.

From 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., families can take short, docent-led gallery tours through the Museum Studios family program. Visitors can participate in Nature in Layers, an art activity for children connected to the museum's exhibitions. Guests can also tour the museum's summer exhibitions, including James Prosek: At Work in the Holmes Gallery and Jill Nathanson: Chromatic Phrases in the Schumann and Titelman galleries.

Second Saturday includes free museum admission throughout the day. Coastal Connections was founded in 2017 with a mission of advancing the survival of sea turtles by educating and connecting people to the environment. Kendra Bergman, founder and executive director of Coastal Connections, said the partnership with the museum is an example of working with the community to introduce marine conservation and environmental protection in unique ways.

cards.headline: Big Taste of Martin County fundraiser to support Big Brothers Big Sisters mentoring programs Oct. 6
cards.teaser: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties will hold its Big Taste of Martin County fundraiser on Oct. 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart.
cards.body:
Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties is preparing for the return of Big Taste of Martin County, a food and spirits event scheduled for Oct. 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart. The annual fundraiser brings together local restaurants, chefs and community partners to support mentoring programs for children across the Treasure Coast.

Guests can sample food, wine and beer from area businesses while participating restaurants compete for Big Taste awards and local bragging rights. The event helps fund mentorship opportunities for children who are currently waiting to be matched with a mentor, known as a Big. Spritz Stuart plans to feature several menu items during the event, including a Tuscan salmon dish, a smash burger and a specialty cocktail called the Fig & Flame.

Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties serves children and families throughout Palm Beach and Martin counties through one-on-one mentoring relationships designed to support academic achievement, confidence and personal growth. Community members can support the mission by purchasing tickets, attending the event or volunteering to become a mentor.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Recreation Department to present 52nd Aerial Antics Youth Circus at St. Edwards School
cards.teaser: The Vero Beach Recreation Department will present 2016 Takeover, the 52nd Aerial Antics Youth Circus, on July 30, July 31 and Aug. 1 at St. Edwards School in Vero Beach.
cards.body:
Vero Beach Recreation Department will present 2016 Takeover, the 52nd Aerial Antics Youth Circus, at St. Edwards School, 1895 Saint Edwards Drive, Vero Beach on Thursday, July 30, Friday, July 31 and Saturday, Aug. 1. The performances are part of the department's summer programming.

Tickets are $8 for adults, $7 for children and seniors, and free for children under 5. The annual youth circus program showcases performances by local young people who have trained throughout the summer. Community members can purchase tickets or get more information by calling 772-770-6500 or 772-978-4500.

cards.headline: Downtown Business Association of Stuart hosts free Rockn Riverwalk concert series every Sunday
cards.teaser: The Downtown Business Association of Stuart is inviting the public to enjoy Rockn Riverwalk, a free open-air concert series held every Sunday on the Riverwalk Stage.

The Downtown Business Association of Stuart is inviting the public to enjoy Rockn Riverwalk, a free open-air concert series held every Sunday on the Riverwalk Stage on St. Lucie Avenue in Stuart. The concerts begin at 1 p.m. and take place on the waterfront, offering live music in an outdoor setting.

The ongoing series provides residents and visitors with a weekly opportunity to enjoy outdoor entertainment along the Stuart waterfront. The free concerts are part of the Downtown Business Association's efforts to bring community programming to the historic downtown area.

cards.body:
